# @uptimizr/react

> Embeddable React analytics panels for an Uptimizr collector, and the single source of truth for
> the OSS dashboard's panel set (ADR 0047). Panels read the collector's query API through a shared
> `CollectorApi` — browser → query API only, never the database. Babylon and the LLM runtime are
> optional, code-split peers, so the core entry stays tree-shakeable.

## Docs

- [Package reference](./README.md): usage, the export table, the portable catalog, Tailwind setup, the assistant.
- [Agent guide](./AGENTS.md): entry points, the panel contract, the assistant options, and the rules an agent must follow.
- [Custom panels guide](https://uptimizr.com/docs/guides/custom-panels/): authoring a `PanelDefinition`.
- [Assistant guide](https://uptimizr.com/docs/guides/assistant/): the in-browser analytics assistant.
- [Query API reference](https://uptimizr.com/docs/api/query/): every endpoint a panel can read.
- [Architecture Decision Records](https://github.com/RaananW/Uptimizr/tree/main/docs/adr): privacy model (0003), extensible dashboard panels (0036), viewer-configurable panels (0039), runtime remote panels (0041), react owns the OSS panel catalog (0047), replay + live presence + portable panels (0049), in-browser analytics assistant (0050), AI-first analytics layer (0051).

## Entry points

- `@uptimizr/react` — provider, hooks, `CollectorApi`, the panel contract, the OSS catalog and views.
- `@uptimizr/react/panels-3d` — Babylon-backed 3D views (`WorldHeatmap3DView`, `ClickRays3DView`, `SessionReplayView`, …); the only entry that pulls 3D view modules into your graph.
- `@uptimizr/react/assistant` — `AssistantPanel`, `useAssistant` (opt-in, code-split).

## Key exports

- Connection: `UptimizrProvider`, `useUptimizr`, `useOptionalUptimizr`, `useCollectorApi`, `CollectorApi`, `CollectorClientKind` (sent as `x-uptimizr-client` for the audit log).
- Ready-made panels: `SessionsPanel`, `PointerHeatmapPanel`, `ViewDirectionHeatmapPanel`, `PerformanceSummaryPanel`.
- Catalog: `ossPanelCatalog` plus every panel individually (`topMeshesPanel`, `worldHeatmapPanel`, `flowPanel`, `livePresencePanel`, `sessionReplayPanel`, `sceneHealthScorePanel`, …) and the view bodies (`TopMeshesView`, `FloorPlanHeatmapView`, `PointerHeatmapView`, `SceneHealthScoreView`, …). `scene-health` is a raw event-count overview; `scene-health-score` is the `insight_scene_health` primitive (ADR 0051 §4) read through `CollectorApi.sceneHealth()` — one 0-100 score per scene over six weighted factors normalised against the project's own preceding window, each bar annotated with the metric id behind it (50 is the project norm, not a pass mark; a `null` factor score renders empty rather than as zero).
- Panel contract: `definePanel`, `PANEL_CONTRACT_VERSION`, types `PanelDefinition` / `PanelContext` / `PanelActions` / `PanelLive` / `PanelCapabilities` / `PanelSurface` / `PanelSpan` / `PanelSettingSpec`; `usePanelData`, `PanelCard`, `PanelMessage`.
- Panel settings (ADR 0039): `resolvePanelSettings`, `coercePanelSetting`, `pruneDefaultOverrides`, `createLocalStoragePanelStore`, `memoryPanelStore`, `EMPTY_PANEL_STATE`.
- Remote panels (ADR 0041): `fetchPanelManifest`, `loadRemotePanels`, `mergePanels`, `isPanelDefinition`, `isPanelManifest`, `isContractCompatible`.
- Pinned panel specs (ADR 0051 §7): `loadSpecPanels(api)` → `{ panels, errors, rows }` fetches the project's pinned panels and turns each into a `PanelDefinition`, mirroring `loadRemotePanels` down to the `RemotePanelError` shape — an invalid spec is reported and skipped, and nothing throws. `specPanel(row)` builds one panel with id `spec:<id>` (`SPEC_PANEL_ID_PREFIX`, `specPanelId`, `isSpecPanelId`, `specIdFromPanelId`) and the spec's `note` as its subtitle; `specQuery(spec, active)` resolves `range: "inherit"` against the filter bar's window on every load; `resolveEncoding(spec)` fills open channels from the metric's label/axis/measure columns; `SpecChart` draws the rows (`SpecChartProps`, `SpecRow`, `LoadSpecPanelsResult`, `SpecPanelData`). A spec is **data** — a metric id, a chart name, some column names — rendered with panels this package already ships, so nothing is imported and nothing is evaluated and ADR 0041's trust decision is untouched. `@uptimizr/metrics` is a direct dependency for the chart/grain rules.
- Panel spec API: `CollectorApi.query(queryV1)` (the GET form of `/api/v1/query`, `format` defaulting to `full`), `.panels()`, `.pinPanel(spec)`, `.updatePanel(id, spec)`, `.unpinPanel(id)`, plus the `PanelSpecRow` type. The read needs `query`; the three writes need `annotate`.
- Filters + live: `DEFAULT_FILTERS`, `TIME_PRESETS`, `INPUT_SOURCES`, `resolveRange`, `toQueryParams`, `annotationTargetFor` (the annotation target implied by the active filters), `pickInterval`, `formatSource`, `useLiveSession`, `useSessionTail`, `LivePresenceView`.
- Project metadata (ADR 0051 §5): `CollectorApi.whoami`, `.annotations`/`.createAnnotation`/`.deleteAnnotation`, `.glossary`/`.defineTerm`, `.analyses`/`.saveAnalysis`, with the `WhoAmI`/`AnnotationRow`/`GlossaryRow`/`SavedAnalysisRow` types. These are the client's only writes: metadata, never events, and each needs a key holding `annotate`.
- Drawing helpers: `drawPointerHeatmap`, `drawDirectionHeatmap`, `heatRgb`, `HEAT_GRADIENT`, `percentileMax`, `heatColor`, `formatNumber`, `formatTime`, `parseTimestamp`.
- Spatial labels (ADR 0051 §2): `api.sceneRegions(sceneId)` reads a scene's named boxes (`[]` when it has none); `voxelHoverLabels(voxels, cellSize, regions, meshes, extra?)` and `labelWorldPoint(x, y, z, regions, meshes, threshold)` resolve the region label and the nearest proxy mesh client-side and feed `WorldHeatmap3DView`'s `voxelLabels`, so the world/gaze/perf/error/boundary 3D panels name a voxel on hover. Same rules as the collector's `format=summary` labelling; regions are keyed per scene, so "All scenes" gets `[]`.
- Assistant subpath: `AssistantPanel` (with `annotationTarget` and `onPinned`), `useAssistant` (adds `canAnnotate`, `annotate`, `saveAnalysis`, `lastReads`, plus `pinnableQuery` — the query behind the last answer, or `null` — and `pinPanel(title, note?)`), `panelSpecForQuery(query, title, note?)` (the pure derivation of a spec from a query, for previewing or testing a pin), `DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, `composeSystemPrompt`, `refreshSystemPrompt`, `DEFAULT_ASSISTANT_MAX_STEPS`.

## Optional peers

`@babylonjs/core`, `@babylonjs/loaders` (3D panels) and `@mlc-ai/web-llm` (the local assistant
backend) are declared **optional** and loaded lazily — add them only if you render a 3D panel or
run a local model.
